chapter: Capitol Records and "On the Street Where You Live"
title: Getting out of the Victor contract to sign with Capitol's Dave Cavanaugh
summary: Irv Jerome brought Dave Cavanaugh to hear him; Burke got Victor to release him as 'a big fish in a small pond', and Jones notes how agents maneuver without telling musicians.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now, here comes '57, we scuffkalong through that. '57 comes, Irv Jerome, Jerry Jerome's brother, he's got Epic, which was a subsidiary to Victor at this time.
It was Columbia.
Huh?
Epic.
Yeah. What did they have as a subsidiary to Victor, sounded like Epic to me, but could have been something else.
Well, Groove was --
Groove was Victor.
Groove was Victor, but Epic was Columbia.
Well, what about Capitol?
Capitol I didn't think had one.

Yeah, they had one and Irv Jerome was head of it. I don't think it was once. Irv Jerome. Well, I know Irv good -- I mean Jerry good. Jerry used to take me on gigs, you know, me and Tyree. So now Irv come in and one night he was in and we was talking and the people was enjoying it, you know, enjoying the music, so he says, 'You know what? Dave Cavanaugh's in town from California. I'm going to have him to come in here and listen to you one night, you know. Can't ever tell what will happen, you know.' I said, 'Yeah. I remember when Dave used to play tenor sax years ago.' He said, 'Yeah, well he's with Capitol now.' So me come in and we got to talking and, 'Who are you with?' I said Victor. He said, 'Oh, yeah, I heard that album.' He says, 'Tell your agent I think that we can do a better job on you. But you know, just tell him that I think I
can do a better one. I don't know what kind of contract you've got or if you've got one. Tell him I think we can do a better job."

Now, he has to go to his boss and try to get -- so he calls Dave and asks Dave did he mean what he told me. So Dave says yeah. He says, "I think we can do a better job on him." So now Sammy's got to go to his man and tell him that Jonah wants to get out of the contract." I don't even know what's happening, you know. I'm glad to have anything, you know. He said, "Jonah wants to get out of the contract." He said, "What's the matter? We only did it once. Give us a chance to make another album." He says, "Well, he feels like he'd rather be a big fish in a little pond than a little fish in a big pond." And they talked. Well, they were boys, you know, and they knew each other for years, and he'd rather be on a smaller label, you know, he'd feel better. It's too heavy for him over here. And so after he talked to him, he said, "Okay. If he's not happy I'll give him his contract back." I didn't even know what they were talking about, didn't even know they was talking. But agents do these things, you know.
Yeah.
But Sammy's a great guy for coming back and telling me what he has to do --
Yeah.
-- to maneuver these things, you know.
Keeps you --
Makes me feel good about it, you know.
Sure.
The guy don't do nothing, he comes back and tells me everything, you know.
Yeah.
